newsitem.title: USA: BROOKLYN UNION, LILCO HOLDERS APPROVE MERGER.
newsitem.headline: BROOKLYN UNION, LILCO HOLDERS APPROVE MERGER.

text.p: Brooklyn Union Gas Co and Long Island Lighting Co said on Thursday their shareholders approved the merger of the two companies into an energy holding company at separate meetings.

LILCO said its shareholders also approved its pact with the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) under which LIPA would acquire LILCO's electric transmission and distribution system, substantially all of its electric regulatory assets and its 18 percent interest in Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear power plant.

LIPA would also assume or refinance a total of about $4 billion in debt and preferred stock, the companies said. Brooklyn Union/LILCO would receive net cash proceeds of about $1.7 billion that would be used to grow the new company.

Brooklyn Union and LILCO announced plans to merge in December, creating a $4 billion electric and gas company. The merger had been conditioned upon approval of each company's shareholders and various regulatory agencies.
The companies said the LIPA transaction, coupled with the merger, was expected to reduce the electric bills of people on Long Island, N.Y. by about 17 percent.
The merger would also provide a two percent cut in natural gas rates for LILCO and Brooklyn Union customers, they said.
Brooklyn Union said its shareholders also approved the formation of an energy holding company -- KeySpan Energy Corp -- as an interim step toward the merger with LILCO.
KeySpan would be created by exchanging shares of Brooklyn Union stock for an equal number of KeySpan shares, it said.
Brooklyn Union Chairman Robert Catell said: "It (the merger) is the logical outcome of intense planning to capitalize on the growth opportunities available in a deregulated environment.
Catell said the merger gave Brooklyn Union access to a million additional customers in an attractive market area.
The companies said they were still in the process of seeking approvals from regulatory agencies.

If the three-way transaction involving LILCO, LIPA and the KeySpan became effective, LILCO shareholders would own about 68 percent of the combined company, and KeySpan holders would own about 32 percent, they said.
